lines.text: Islands in the Indian Ocean, empty until the eighteenth century, now home to a small nation and giant tortoises. This is the Seychelles.
In 1778 French settlers founded a town on the island of Mahe. Today it is Victoria, one of the smallest capitals in the world.
France-Albert Rene, born in 1935, would take power in 1977 and rule for more than a quarter of a century.
James Mancham, born in 1939, would become the first president, until he was overthrown.
James Michel, born in 1944, would follow Rene as president in 2004.
Wavel Ramkalawan, born in 1961, would be elected president in 2020.
And Patrick Herminie, born in 1963, became president in 2025.
In 1976 the Seychelles became independent from Britain, a nation of more than a hundred islands. A year later, Mancham was overthrown.
In 1981 a band of foreign mercenaries tried to seize the islands. The coup failed.
In 1982 the atoll of Aldabra, home to some hundred thousand giant tortoises, was named a World Heritage Site.
A year later the Vallee de Mai joined it, a palm forest where the giant coco de mer grows.
From an empty archipelago to a nation that guards its wild treasures, the Seychelles story is young.
